when_to_use: golden-era jazz rap where a chopped Rhodes loop feels archival but the drum pocket and muted-horn replies keep rewriting its present meaning, 84-88 BPM

defaults.feel: humanized 16th grid, kick pushed ahead, snare dragged behind, 54-62% hi-hat swing

signature_moves: golden-era loop: Dm9 -> G13 -> Cmaj9 -> A7(b9,b13), balancing warmth with a turnaround that keeps the story unfinished
chill descending loop: Fmaj9 -> Em7 -> Dm9 -> Cmaj9, creating the sense of a sample settling deeper into itself
dark urban minor: Am9 -> D9 -> Fmaj7 -> E7alt, opening one shadowed harmonic corner before the beat returns to familiarity
rootless shells: let the harmony instrument carry only guide tones and extensions so bass owns the ground and the sample remains uncluttered
cadence_options: loop turnaround on an altered dominant so the last bar feels like a hand pulling the listener back to bar 1
no final cadence when the strongest ending is the loop being removed, filtered, or abandoned mid-memory
avoid: doubling the bass root in the Rhodes or piano low register, which removes space and sample-like separation
quantized or symmetrical drums; the identity is the intentional disagreement between kick, snare, and hat

hook_archetypes.name: smoke-at-the-loop-edge
hook_archetypes.rhythm: a short 1-2 bar horn phrase placed near the end of a 4-bar loop so it behaves like commentary, not continuous melody
hook_archetypes.contour: a muted trumpet or tenor line that descends or curls into the next downbeat, sounding observant rather than triumphant
hook_archetypes.first_appears: Hook or Chorus, after the listener already knows the Rhodes loop and can hear the horn changing its perspective

hook_archetypes.name: one-word-scar
hook_archetypes.rhythm: a single vocal chop or syllable used as an off-beat punctuation mark, never as a full sung line
hook_archetypes.contour: minimal pitch content; identity comes from placement, repetition, and one later omission
hook_archetypes.first_appears: Hook or Chorus beneath the horn response, then withheld once so its absence becomes noticeable

intro.note_lengths: sparse or absent; let the filtered loop feel like a source being discovered before anyone speaks over it

verse.note_lengths: conversational phrases with few sustained notes, leaving bars where rhythm section and text can breathe
verse.contour: pitch movement remains secondary to cadence, repetition, and verbal weight
verse.placement: laid-back and dragged, with the lead functioning as the loosest voice in the pocket

hook.note_lengths: one compact muted-horn phrase and selective vocal-chop accents; repetition should feel iconic rather than constant
hook.contour: smoky and understated, with one target that points into the next loop instead of closing the phrase
hook.placement: behind the beat, landing near the loop boundary

breakdown.note_lengths: sparse and exposed after the drums disappear; allow the remaining soloist to leave incomplete thoughts
breakdown.contour: open register and wider rests, creating distance from the verse without inventing a new song
breakdown.placement: rubato-adjacent, the loosest point of the arrangement

drum_skeleton.low_energy: a foundational boom-bap pattern with kick on 1 and selected off-beats, snare dragged behind beats 2 and 4 with one soft ghost, and hats in steady 8ths; the pocket should feel heavy before it feels busy
drum_skeleton.mid_energy: move hats toward 16ths, thicken ghost snares around the 2-and-4 backbeat, and add a kick pickup only where it increases dialogue with the sample
drum_skeleton.high_energy: increase internal ghost activity and selective open-hat accents while preserving the audible push-pull; density must never erase the lurch
drum_skeleton.optional_half_time_variant: for a deliberate half-time passage only, move the primary snare to beat 3 and label the section half-time explicitly - never call this the standard pocket

arrangement_defaults.layout_rules: begin with the Rhodes loop sounding found rather than introduced. Drums and sub-bass turn the artifact into a present-tense pocket. Let the verse voice occupy space without covering the loop. Every 8 bars, remove drums briefly so the sample shows its age and fragility. Bring the horn only after the groove is established, as commentary from the edge of the frame. The bridge should strip to loop, sub, and one solo voice. End by filtering or withdrawing the loop so the track feels like it continues somewhere beyond the file.

anti_boredom_rules: the drum push-pull must remain audible at every energy level; density cannot flatten the relationship between kick, snare, and hat
keep the harmonic loop short and hypnotic; develop through filtering, subtraction, response, bass character, and orchestration rather than longer progression
include at least one complete drum dropout before the final hook or outro so the return of the pocket has meaning
the horn hook must recur with a changed register, ending, response, or absence
keep the harmony instrument rootless so the bass remains the sole owner of the ground and the loop stays open

bass_behavior.role: sub-bass root authority under rootless samples
bass_behavior.rhythmic_relationship: selectively locks with the ahead-of-grid kick and leaves space around dragged snares
bass_behavior.density: sparse sustained roots with occasional approach notes
bass_behavior.articulation: long notes with controlled cutoffs before crowded drum events

groove_intent.feel: asymmetric boom-bap push-pull on a swung-sixteenth grid
groove_intent.kick: slightly ahead with variable syncopated placement
groove_intent.snare: behind beats 2 and 4 in regular time
groove_intent.hihat: uneven swung eighths or sixteenths with velocity variation
groove_intent.ensemble_relationship: sub-bass locks selectively with kick while Rhodes and lead sit farther back
optional_variants: explicitly labeled half-time section with primary snare on beat 3

distinguishing_traits: rootless sampled Rhodes loop with sub-bass ownership of roots
muted horn and vocal chops punctuate a verse-hook hip-hop form
